answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with escalating identity stakes: the first identity locks a small refundable deposit, each further identity from the same operator costs progressively more, like rings cut from one cedar trunk. A non-transferable reputation pigment, earned only through verified completed work, marks genuine history, and random sparrow checks challenge sampled agents with live proof-of-work. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand work histories, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
